column1: # One program's rows of the -db fixtures (see README.md here for the columns and the loader in ../db_search_fixtures.py).
# Rows db.sa.*.5 (OF4a): -outfmt 5 (BLAST XML) of BLASTN and BLASTP, each the search of the db.sa.*.8 row of the same stem (stdout is the XML document; hit ids gnl|BL_ORD_ID|N).

# Rows db.sa.*.1[56], db.x16.* and db.x16_*taxid.* (OF5a for BLASTP and BLASTN, OF5b for BLASTX, TBLASTN and TBLASTX): -outfmt 16 (BLAST XML2) and 15 (BLAST JSON) of all five programs, the search of the .5 or .8 row of the same stem where the covers cell says so; BLASTDB=DIR, BATCH_SIZE=N, ARCHIVE_FORMAT=X and PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=N tokens in extra_args are environment variables of the NCBI run and of LOSAT's.

# Rows db.sa.* (line OF, OF3b): -outfmt 8 (Seq-annot, ASN.1 text) and 12 (Seq-annot, JSON) and, in the ids ending .9 (OF3c), 9 (Seq-annot, binary ASN.1; the fixture files are binary, see fixtures/db_search/.gitattributes); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sa.`.

# Rows db.sa.*.1[34] (OF5c, BLASTP and BLASTN): -outfmt 14 and 13 (side files and a master file) of the search of the .16/.15 row of the same stem. The files column is xinclude: the runner adds `-out <tmp>/<row_id>.out`; the master is frozen as <row_id>.out (stdout_sha256, stdout_bytes; standard output is empty), the side files as <row_id>.out_<n>.xml|json (side_sha256, in order). A row of the old form has 12 cells and no files columns (LOSAT/tests/xinclude_fixtures.py).

# Rows db.numdesc.* (line NP, O1b): -num_descriptions and -num_alignments (blast_args.cpp:2894-2973); the last one is NCBI's error for a hit list size of 0 (rc 1, empty stdout); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.numdesc.`.
# Rows db.blastp.culling_* and db.tblastn.culling_* (line NP, O3b): -culling_limit with -db; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.blastp.culling_` / `--only db.tblastn.culling_`.

# Rows db.sc4a.* (line NP, series SC, SC4a): BLASTP -comp_based_stats 0 with -db: AMRFinderPlus's protein search (amrfinder.cpp 4.2.7, the options of seq.hpp's blastp_fast set and its 10-column tabular report) of the 89 proteins of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa against paja, and the steps after the ordinary traceback (hit list size, culling, query coverage, a query cut into chunks, -query_loc).

# Rows db.sc4a.cbs0.*, db.sc4a.q1.6, db.sc4a.q119.6, db.sc4a.amr_q119.6 (drop-in DI-3): the same mode with -db in outfmt 0, 5 and 7, with one query (tests/fasta/outfmt0/sc4a_q1.faa, the first record of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa) and 119 queries (tests/fasta/LvMJNV.faa).
# Rows db.sc4a.gap.* (drop-in DI-3): the same mode against stored - (tests/db_search/gapmix, DI-12's rows db.gap.*).

# Rows db.sc2a.* (line NP, series SC, SC2a): BLASTP with BLOSUM62 and gap costs of its table other than 11/1 with -db (tests/db_search/paja, a split query against tests/seqdb/db/prot_v4) in composition modes 2 and 0 and with -task blastp-fast; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sc2a.`.

# Rows db.sc3.* (line NP, series SC, SC3): BLASTP -task blastp-short and -word_size 2 with -db: the short queries of tests/fasta/outfmt0/sc3_short_q.faa and the 89 proteins of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa against tests/db_search/paja, composition mode 0, the one-hit search, culling, PAM30, blastp-fast, and a query split into chunks (tests/db_search/split_q.faa against tests/seqdb/db/prot_v4). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --only db.sc3.

# Rows db.sc8a.* (line NP, series SC, SC8a): BLASTP -word_size 6 and 7 (the compressed lookup table, BLOSUM62) with -db: the 89 proteins of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa and the 4 of tests/fasta/outfmt0/sc4a_q.faa against paja, both tasks, -mt_mode 1, -query_loc, SEG with soft masking, a query cut into chunks.

# Rows db.sc8b.* (line NP, series SC, SC8b): BLASTP -word_size 4 (the lookup table of words of 4) with -db: the 89 proteins of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa, the 4 of tests/fasta/outfmt0/sc4a_q.faa and the short queries of SC3 against paja, -task blastp, blastp-fast and blastp-short, BLOSUM45, composition mode 0, the one-hit search and a query cut into chunks (tests/db_search/split_q.faa against tests/seqdb/db/prot_v4). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --only db.sc8b.

# Rows db.tm.* (line DBID, item T): NCBI's messages about the taxonomy database (BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/<variant>) in the formats that prefetch the reported subjects (outfmt 0, 5, 6, 7, 17), all five programs: the open messages (bad_magic, count_larger), the volume lookup of a taxid at the last index entry (offset_last_past_end, databases x16_*taxid_99990), several batches (BATCH_SIZE=100), a batch whose first queries have warnings of their own (x16_*qinv: letters that give no Karlin-Altschul parameters, a query without letters), a database with parsed Seq-ids, and a taxonomy database without messages (good). Review 1 (db.tm.bp.fast.*, db.tm.bp.2vol.*, db.tm.*.cache*): blastp-fast with two query blocks (tests/db_search/tm_fast_q289.faa), an alias of two volumes (tests/db_search/tm_2vol), and the volumes tm_cache150 (refused: a taxid of the slot of the offset error's taxid in NCBI's per-volume taxonomy cache) and tm_cache151 (its control); tests/db_search/README.md says how they were made. Item P1 (db.tm.psi.*, db.tm.bp.off0.*): psiblast's prefetch of its traceback hit lists (tests/db_search/tm_psi: a subject beyond -max_target_seqs 1), one query per batch, and PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT turning the prefetch off (0, or below the batch's Seq-aligns: lim6 against lim7; fields that read no subject: qe), blastp too; review 1: subjects beyond the cut whose Seq-align id is found nowhere (tm_psi_pig), fails (tm_psi_rz) or is held by another sequence (tm_psi_held: no taxid, no lookup; tm_psi_held2: taxid 99990, refused). Item P2 (db.tm.{bn,tn,bx,tx}.off0.*, db.tm.tn.lim*, db.tm.tx.lim1.*, db.tm.{bn,bx}.ug.*): PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT turning the prefetch off in BLASTN, TBLASTN, BLASTX and TBLASTX: the messages after the warnings of the query whose report fetches (x16_*qinv), none for fields that read no subject (qe; BLASTN's formatter also for nident), outfmt 5 (warnings in the Iteration messages), the volume lookup once per volume and taxid (lastoff), and the batch's Seq-aligns at the limit: one per HSP of a gapped search (tblastn lim2 against lim3), one per subject of an ungapped one (tblastx lim1, blastn and blastx -ungapped lim2); review 1: the subject's frame with a coordinate field in the translated programs (frame, sframe), and a run whose batches never prefetch and whose fields read no subject on tm_cache150 (not refused).

# Rows db.im.* (line DBID P3): PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=2147483647, at which NCBI's s_PreFetchSeqs prefetches before it tests the format (blast_app_util.cpp:738-740), so also for the Seq-annots outfmt 8, 9 and 12 (not the archive, written without the prefetch): the taxonomy database's messages of db.tm.* after the reader's messages (BLASTN, TBLASTN, BLASTX, TBLASTX, BLASTP), the variable unset as a control, and the subjects with parsed Seq-ids that the prefetch reads by their Seq-align ids: lcl|777 before gi|777 without and with a Seq-align whose length the prefetch asks for; losat-rejection: a lookup that fails, another sequence whose definition lines do not hold the id (NCBI exit 2; also psiblast's list beyond -max_target_seqs, which NCBI prefetches at any value) and copies whose texts depend on the copy NCBI reads (as in outfmt 6).

# Rows db.tab.bp.* and db.tab.bx.* (line CLI, C2, PR 3): BLASTP and BLASTX custom tabular reports (-outfmt "6|7|10|20 [delim=X] <fields>") with -db: every identifier, alignment and taxonomy field on databases with and without -parse_seqids and with taxids (ids/prot_v5, ids/prot_v4, x16_taxid, paja), outfmt 10 and 20, delim= forms, NCBI's delimiter error (rc 1, stderr only), -query_loc (BLASTP only; the BLASTX -query_loc rows with -db are db.bxloc.*), the Galaxy and nf-core calls (corpus GAL10, NFC07) and the ABRicate call (X04); the -subject rows are tab.bp.* and tab.bx.* in outfmt0_manifest.tsv, the taxonomy database names are db.tab.names.*. Freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.tab.bp.` / `freeze --only db.tab.bx.`.

# Rows db.tab.names.* (line CLI, C2, PR 3): the taxonomy database names (ssciname scomname sblastname sskingdom and the plural sscinames scomnames sblastnames sskingdoms) of BLASTN, BLASTP and BLASTX with -db and BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/<variant> (the db.tm.* variants): the good database (outfmt 6, 10 and 20; a scientific name with quotes, a comma and a semicolon: taxid 7777), a taxid that the database does not know (taxdb_xml2/no_9606), NCBI's open message (bad_magic), empty fields, the volume lookup and offset error of the last index entry (offset_last_past_end, databases x16_*taxid_99990), and a parsed database with taxids (ids/prot_v5); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.tab.names.`.

# Rows db.tf.* (DI-8a, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -taxids, -taxidlist, -negative_taxids, -negative_taxidlist and -no_taxid_expansion with -db on the version 5 databases of tests/db_search/taxfilter (tfp protein, tfn nucleotide in two volumes; make_taxfilter.py), the taxonomy file taxfilter/taxonomy4blast.sqlite3 by the BLASTDB=DIR token; db.tf.*.empty.6 are LOSAT refusals of a list that excludes every OID (NCBI searches an empty database).

# Rows db.gis.* (dropin DI-7): -show_gis on databases with parsed Seq-ids (ids/prot_v5, prot_v4, nucl_v5, nucl_v4: every Seq-id form, GIs, several definition lines): outfmt 0 shows gi|N| and the FASTA form of the id; outfmt 5 and 6, and a database without parsed Seq-ids, do not change.

# Rows db.sl.* (DI-8b, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -seqidlist and -negative_seqidlist with -db on the version 5 databases tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp and tfn (two volumes) and tests/db_search/ids/prot_v5 and nucl_v5 (every Seq-id form), the version 4 databases ids/prot_v4 and nucl_v4 (string ISAM), with the lists of tests/db_search/seqidlist (make_seqidlist.py: text lists in NCBI's token forms, binary lists in blastdb_aliastool's format); the negative lists on ids/prot_v5, prot_v4, nucl_v5 and nucl_v4 (db.sl.bp.nforms.6, bp.v4neg.6, bp.v4gi.6, bn.nforms.6, bn.v4neg.6) are LOSAT refusals too: those databases hold sequences whose every definition line has only a gi or a ti, which a negative seqid list leaves without a line (NCBI drops their hits without notice, DI-8b DECISIONS 17); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sl.`.

# Rows db.sp.* (dropin DI-7): -searchsp with -db (the five programs): the effective search space of the E-values, the cutoffs, `Effective search space used:`, Statistics_eff-space and the archive; -dbsize stays in the length adjustment; NCBI sets OLD_FSC at any -searchsp value (blast_args.cpp:303-307), so the protein programs lose the Gumbel block.

# Rows db.oldfsc.* (line SW, env parity G1): the environment variable OLD_FSC (any value, the empty one too), with which NCBI's protein programs have no Gumbel block (blast_stat.c:921-923): the E-values and cutoffs without the finite-size correction, as with `-searchsp 0` (NCBI sets OLD_FSC for any -searchsp, blast_args.cpp:303-307) but with the archive's options of a search without -searchsp; -ungapped frees the block anyway (blast_setup.c:521-527; BLASTX, the program of these three that LOSAT searches ungapped). BLASTP, BLASTX, TBLASTN, PSIBLAST (PS5c) and RPSBLAST (PS11c-2, rows db.rps.mini.oldfsc.* in rpsblast.tsv) read it (`old_fsc`).

# Rows db.acbs.* (line SW, env parity G2+G3): the environment variable ADAPTIVE_CBS (any value, the empty one too), with which NCBI's protein programs keep a larger preliminary hit list with composition-based statistics (blast_hits.c:43-70) and, for a hit list size below 1000, cut it by E-value when the stream closes (BlastHSPCBSStreamClose, blast_hspstream.c:816-864; not PSIBLAST, whose traceback size is the preliminary size): tests/db_search/acbs and acbs_n (README.md there), the 1,050 vs 1,500 lists of 700 composition-biased and 1,000 ordinary subjects; rows near/wrap/crash: -max_target_seqs whose preliminary size passes NCBI's int (BLASTX; NCBI wraps it or crashes), which LOSAT computes without the overflow (PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS exception 19, line O1c): each is compared with NCBI's run at 1073741798, its `ncbi-near` row near.*.

# Rows db.pd.* (dropin DI-7): -parse_deflines with -db (the five programs): the query ids of Query=, qseqid, qacc, qaccver, qgi, the XML query id and title, the Seq-aligns and the archive (Bioseq ids, seq-loc-list when no id is local); query files of tests/db_search/make_pd.py; losat-rejection rows are LOSAT's refusals of what NCBI's scope shows as another sequence (dropin-survey-20261029/DI7/DECISIONS.md 7, 8).

# Rows db.ec.* (DI-8c, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): a taxid or seqid list that keeps no sequence of the database (tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp, tfn; ids/prot_v4, nucl_v4): NCBI searches nothing, warns `Filtering resulted in an empty database.` for each query of a searched batch and reports its statistics from the length of OID 0 and one sequence; query files of tests/db_search/seqidlist (make_seqidlist.py); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.ec.`.

# Rows db.sa8.* (DI-8d, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): a positive taxid or seqid list writes the `ext` `use_this_seqid` on each Seq-align (outfmt 8, 9, 11, 12; tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp, tfn; useseqid/ for the id forms), limits the outfmt 0 heading to the lines it names; a negative list writes none; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sa8.`.

# Rows db.mdb.* (DI-8f, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -db with several names (`-db "a b"`: one virtual database, as NCBI's CSeqDB) on the databases of tests/db_search/multidb (make_multidb.py): version 5 pairs with taxids (pa pb, na nb; nb and pb hold a copy of a sequence of the other), a version 5 database without -parse_seqids (nnp), version 4 pairs (n4a n4b, p4a p4b), one base name in two directories (d1/g d2/g), an empty title (et), an alias (al), a seqid list (sl.txt); the names given twice, in the other order, in double quotes (Galaxy) and with extra spaces; db.mdb.bn.v4v5.6 is NCBI's exit 2 for both versions; db.mdb.bn.mixed.6 and db.mdb.bn.aliasdup.0 are LOSAT refusals.

# Rows db.envshared.* (line DBID N2e): blastp, psiblast, tblastn, tblastx and blastn -db with the same environment (blast_app_util.cpp:206-210, 732-737): NCBI's apps but psiblast write the archive of outfmt 11 without the prefetch (blastp_app.cpp:280-285, tblastn_app.cpp:294-299, tblastx_app.cpp:197-202, blastn_app.cpp:304-309), so a PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT that NStr::StringToInt cannot convert leaves it as it is, while psiblast fetches ahead before it writes one (psiblast_app.cpp:262-266); a -db search ignores BL2SEQ_LEGACY; in the other formats the value stops LOSAT as it stops NCBI, with its exception (env parity H; tests/search_environment.rs has the -subject cases).

# Rows db.archtitle.* (line NP, series SM, DECISIONS 20 c (e)): outfmt 11 of the five programs against tests/db_search/arch_snucl (BLASTN), arch_sprot (BLASTP), arch_tbn_snucl (TBLASTN), bslice (BLASTX) and arch_tbx_snucl (TBLASTX), with the query files of fasta_input_fixtures.py's arch_title rows (tests/fixtures/fasta_input/batch_title_*: record 6's CheckDataLine error, `café` on record 5 or 1, or on the last record without letters; batchlong_title_late: BLASTN's mixer; batch_title.s, the subjects of those rows, with `café` on record 2 and no reader error: the clean.zero rows, whose batch size of 0 the library API, which reads the whole query first, meets before a reader error). The archive of each batch that NCBI completes holds its queries; the batch that stops the run (the reader error, a last batch without letters, a batch size of 0) writes none: LOSAT writes the title of a batch NCBI completes as NCBI does: `#` in the archive for each byte the stream replaces, and its `Bad char` report on stderr.

# Rows db.archtitle.*.nosq.* (line NP, series SM, DECISIONS 25): the same rule where NCBI's search fails: arch_sprot_nopsq (BLASTP, BLASTX) and arch_tbn_snucl_nonsq (TBLASTN, BLASTN, TBLASTX) are arch_sprot and arch_tbn_snucl without their sequence file, which NCBI reads first in the preliminary search of the first batch with a valid context and fails there (BLAST engine error: Database memory map file error, rc 3). The queries batch_title_unsearched* hold two records of X (protein) or N (nucleotide) only, u1 and u2, which have no valid context (NCBI does not search their batch but writes its archive), then q3 and q4; `café` is the title of u1 (batch_title_unsearched) or of q3 (batch_title_unsearched_next). .one: the default batch holds every record and fails, so no archive holds u1; .next: with BATCH_SIZE 60 (protein) or 180 (nucleotide) the first batch {u1, u2} is written and the second, with q3, fails; .unsearched: the same batches with `café` on u1, which NCBI writes, with the `Bad char` reports of u1's title on stderr. BLASTP refuses a first batch that NCBI does not search when the database cannot be searched (preliminary_search_error), so it has the .one row only. A missing header file (NCBI's message holds the file's absolute path, not frozen) is in tests/outfmt11_titles.rs.

# Rows db.sc4b.* (line NP, series SC, SC4b): BLASTP -matrix IDENTITY with -db: SicyWSV's 89 queries (the warning for the first batch's 16 only), mode 0, XML, the archive, a query split into chunks; with SC3, blastp-short with the short queries and -word_size 2 with SicyWSV; NCBI's errors (-matrix identity with XML, exit 3; word size 6; gap costs 11/1; psiblast's IDENTITY) and LOSAT's rejection of word size 5 and blastp-fast, on which NCBI 2.17.0 dies of SIGSEGV, except with a first query batch of queries without letters, where NCBI stops with its error (BLASTP and TBLASTN). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --only db.sc4b.

# Rows db.sc5.* (line NP, series SC, SC5): -comp_based_stats 1 and 3 with -db: BLASTP (SicyWSV's 89 queries, BLOSUM45, PAM30, pairwise, the archive, a query split into chunks), psiblast (round 1 in that mode, two rounds: the later round runs 3 as 1 with NCBI's warning) and TBLASTN (PAM70, -db_gencode 2). The rows db.ps.pssm.cbs1.6, db.ps.it.cbs1.pk.6 and db.ps.it.cbs3.pk.6 were the refusal rows db.ps.pssm.rej.cbs1, db.ps.it.rej.cbs1 and db.ps.it.rej.cbs3 until SC5 (the same commands).

# Rows db.sc8c.* (line NP, series SC, SC8c): BLASTP's block search closes a block on the words of its compressed lookup table: with a lowered -threshold the 89 proteins of tests/fasta/SicyWSV.faa are searched in blocks of one NCBI batch each instead of two blocks of letters.

# Rows db.col.* (line SW, SW8 follow-up 2): databases whose volumes have column files, searched without a database mask (-db_soft_mask, -db_hard_mask or an imported search strategy, which LOSAT refuses), for which NCBI opens no column file (tests/db_search/coldb, make_coldb.py: p5m and p4m with the seg masks of segmasker, n5m with those of dustmasker and windowmasker in two volumes, n4m with dustmasker's; dmg/CASE/ copies of p4m and n4m with a damaged column; coldb/ucol/user-column-db, NCBI's database with the user column `comedy`). The ncbi rows are NCBI 2.17.0 `-num_threads 1` on these files, the same bytes as for the files without their columns (the SW8 follow-up probe); db.col.rej.* keep LOSAT's refusal of the mask options.
# Rows db.t1.* (line RG, T1): -sorthits, -sorthsps and -line_length with -db (the -subject rows are t1.* in ../outfmt0_manifest.tsv). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --only db.t1.

# Rows db.envconv.* (env parity H): -db with a CHUNK_SIZE, OVERLAP_CHUNK_SIZE, BATCH_SIZE or PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT that NStr::StringToInt (flags 0) cannot convert: NCBI stops with its CStringException (CATCH_ALL: 'Error: ' and its report naming ncbistr.cpp in the official release's build tree, exit 255) where it reads the value: CHUNK_SIZE and OVERLAP_CHUNK_SIZE in the first batch's query splitter (local_blast.cpp:59-61, split_query_aux_priv.cpp:55-57; blastn reads CHUNK_SIZE first for its mixer), BATCH_SIZE before the formatter (blast_input_aux.cpp:86-88; blastn after PrintProlog, blastn_app.cpp:258-262; psiblast never), PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT before the first batch's report (blast_app_util.cpp:732-734; not with outfmt 11 but in psiblast); with outfmt 11 NCBI writes its error archive (env-parity-20261108/h_probe/REPORT.md).

# Rows db.pd.q1c.* (line RG, series Q, Q1c): -parse_deflines with two queries of one id and with a query whose id a reported database sequence has (tests/db_search/q1c, make_q1c_inputs.py), in two query batches (BATCH_SIZE=1): NCBI's formatter empties its scope after each batch (CBlastFormat::ResetScopeHistory) but in outfmt 5, so NCBI searches each query with its own letters and shows a database sequence with the id of a query of another batch as itself; in one batch and in outfmt 5 LOSAT refuses them (the losat-rejection rows; db.pd.*.dup and db.pd.*.clash: one batch). A refusal of the second of two queries with one id in a later batch comes after the reports of the batches before (line WQA D10 round 4, 2026-11-20): its stdout is NCBI's of the row's near input, whose second lcl|dup2 is a line that NCBI's reader refuses (rows .dup2stop.*, ncbi-near), and an error of NCBI's in the search of a batch before comes first (rows .avgstop.*: subjects of 2, 0 and 0 letters with -searchsp 1000). Rows .avgdup.*, .avgdup2.*, .avglong.*, .kadup.*, .avgearly.* and .avgmid.* (line WQA D10 round 5, 2026-11-20): the batch of the second q1 stops at one point in every program: NCBI's error of the set-up of the batch's records before the second q1 where it fails for the subjects (subjects of 2, 0 and 0 letters, or 2, 0 and 0 nucleotides, with -searchsp 1000; also with a first q1 in a batch before, and with a repeat longer than its first q1 where the batch ends with the input), else LOSAT's refusal. NCBI's reader counts a repeated record into its batch by its first record's letters, and so does LOSAT's at every cut of the batches since round 6 (review 4 of D10): the batch of the second q1 is NCBI's, and its set-up takes the records first in the scope with their own letters (BATCH_SIZE=55 with q1 of 30 X, a second q1 of 20 letters and q2: the batch is the two q1, which NCBI does not search, writing q1's warning twice before its error of q2's batch, so LOSAT refuses it; BATCH_SIZE=30: the second q1 alone). Rows .g2a.*, .g2b.*, .avgmid.one.* and .nosq.* (round 6): g2a, q1 of 60 letters (180 nucleotides), a second q1 of 10 (30) and a line that NCBI's reader refuses, BATCH_SIZE=100 (300): NCBI's first batch is the two q1, searched, then the reader's error, so LOSAT refuses that batch; g2b, 10 then 60 (BATCH_SIZE=50, 150): the batch counts 10 + 10 and reads the refused line, the reader's error first (NCBI's); avgmid in one batch: NCBI's error of the set-up of q1 and q2; q1, q2, q1 in one batch against arch_sprot_nopsq or arch_tbn_snucl_nonsq (no sequence file): the set-up passes and NCBI's first read of the database fails (BLAST engine error: Database memory map file error, exit 3; at outfmt 11 the archive first). A record that -query_loc skips joins the scope (rows .skipcount.*, .skiprep.*): it adds nothing to the batch, and a later q1 counts its letters; BLASTX's scopes take it too, so a q1 after a skipped q1 is refused (NCBI sets it up in the skipped record's letters and stops: CSeqVector_CI: cannot locate segment). Refused also: blastn's repeat longer than its first q1 (NCBI's set-up reads the repeat's own interval in the first record's letters: past their end, CSeqVector_CI: cannot locate segment); a first q1 of only N (NCBI sets up no valid context and exits 0).

# Rows db.of18.* (line RG, T2): -outfmt 18, the organism report, with -db and (db cells subject:PATH) -subject, inputs and NCBI-built databases in ../db_search/of18 (probe T/t2 of line RG), taxonomy databases ../seqdb/taxdb/of18 and of18bl (make_taxdb.py of of18.tsv, of18bl.tsv). Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --only db.of18.

# Rows db.oir.* (line RG, series D, D1a-2 part 2; remaining-gaps-20261112/D/SURVEY_D1a2_A.md): FIRST_OID and LAST_OID of 2^31 or more (NCBI's negative ints) and the iteration range of the only alias file of a -db, alone and with another database (tests/db_search/oidrange: the probe cases p4a_* over taxfilter/tfp, tfn and the database o, ten sequences of tfp under lcl|o0..o9, taxid 10116); -taxids and -seqidlist rows scan the totals over NCBI's loop of the list.
